newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghan Taleban attack, detain Red Cross official.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban attack, detain Red Cross official.

text.p: Taleban militia have attacked and detained a member of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) in the Afghan capital, the ICRC said on Wednesday.

An ICRC spokesman told reporters the delegate was assaulted while walking between two ICRC houses 200 metres apart on Monday night. Several Taleban guards beat him and then took him to the foreign ministry and then to a jail.
Taleban officials were not immediately available for comment.
ICRC sources identified the victim as Swiss national Jean Goude, who supervised detention issues in Kabul.
Goude was released on Tuesday morning, the spokesman said.

"We have sent a letter to the foreign minister in Kabul explaining that it was wrong for the Red Cross to walk at 11 o'clock at night but at the same time we reminded the Taleban about their behaviour, saying it was not right to beat somebody," the spokesman said.
The Taleban took Kabul and three eastern Afghan provinces in a lightning offensive last month.
Many Afghans have welcomed the takeover saying it has brought peace and security, although others have attacked the movement's purist Islamic laws.

The ICRC spokesman said Goude was in poor physical condition on his release, with heavy bruising to the face. He also had difficulty breathing. He has been sent to the Pakistani frontier town of Peshawar for routine checks, the spokesman added.

The spokesman said it was the first time any ICRC official had been assaulted. He said he had requested an answer from the Taleban government and guarantees that all ICRC officials would be protected.
